conclusions: This window's Hyle BF16-score and F32-score policies happen to produce identical64 IDs, rounds/work counters and18record/50reuse. This finite result does not establish mathematical equivalence, general quality or the absence of score differences.

The F32-score Hyle median P/D/session rates are slightly lower; all three before/current ranges overlap. No speed improvement is demonstrated. Cold load/ready/startup ranges also overlap and are not evidence of a reproducible startup win.

cublas-score-next.json.scope: Read-only next-candidate design. No source/API/routing modification, compilation or GPU execution.
cublas-score-next.json.conclusion: Yes. The existing BFloatLinearF32 public operation can be admitted by the existing cuBLASLt provider, using BF16 A/B descriptors and F32 C/D descriptors, the original QueueSequence/Completion/workspace mechanism and prepared native artifact. A new public operation, consumer provider branch or executor is unnecessary.

current_facts.fact: select_layouts admits only ordinary MatMul with F32 accumulation and matching dtype across both inputs and output. Current provider therefore rejects the mixed-output custom operation.
BatchGeometry has one element_bytes; configure creates every A/B/C layout using one CUDA dtype. Extending operation admission alone would leave F32 output byte span and descriptor dtype incorrect.

Cold heuristics/descriptors and a bounded caller workspace already exist. Runtime is shared-queue, prepared, non-host-blocking, capture-compatible, with separate mutable handle/workspace per Invocation. Submit uses actual QueueSequence and reports possible accepted work even on the first vendor error.

Ordinary rank-2 plain MatMul receives the existing general cuBLAS preference. Unrecognized custom operations currently receive the ggml baseline; adding cuBLAS capability alone is not evidence the default planner will select it.

minimal_provider_change.part: Operation admission and unchanged ordinary contract
minimal_provider_change.change: Include model_ops.h, branch on the existing BFloatLinearF32 type in select_layouts and use its inference to validate dense rank-2 BF16 [T,K], BF16 stored [E,K], F32 [T,E]. Ordinary MatMul keeps matching-type admission, existing broadcast rules and F32 accumulation unchanged. Do not reinterpret arbitrary mixed-dtype MatMul as this operation.

The stored weight remains the original row-major [E,K] BF16 allocation. A minimal reuse of existing non-transposed native layout machinery is to describe those exact bytes as column-major [K,E] with leading=K (swap the native rows/columns and order, preserve pointer/leading), so A[T,K] times B_native[K,E] produces C[T,E]. Equivalent opB=T with physical row-major [E,K] is legal in principle but requires carrying/configuring the transpose descriptor consistently. Select one representation, not both.
minimal_provider_change.bounds: Validate semantic shapes against original tensor descriptors first. Native storage-span calculation for COL[K,E] must still equal physical E*K elements. No transpose kernel, repack, copied vocabulary bank, token/model name or provider branch in Recipe.scores.

minimal_provider_change.change: Replace the private single element_bytes assumption with exact A/B/C port widths and native dtypes (BF16=2, BF16=2, F32=4 for this operation; C and D share the output descriptor). Use each port width for storage span/overflow checks, whole-element batch stride admission and CUBLASLT_MATRIX_LAYOUT_STRIDED_BATCH_OFFSET. configure_run creates layout i using dtype[i].
minimal_provider_change.bounds: matrix_layout already derives leading dimensions using the actual TensorDesc dtype; preserve that. Output leading is E F32 elements / 4*E bytes, not half the F32 extent. Keep original offset/alignment/non-overlap checks and INT domain checks for every port. This custom operation is rank-2: do not invent batched custom syntax or broaden its public contract.

minimal_provider_change.change: Keep the existing BF16 input computation policy CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F and F32 alpha/beta scale type. A/B remain CUDA_R_16BF; C/D are CUDA_R_32F. Do not select compute policy solely from output dtype and unintentionally change BF16 Tensor Core arithmetic to the ordinary F32-input PEDANTIC policy. Existing split-K reduction mask retains F32 partial sums.

Reuse one cold configure/create_runs path, alignment preference, actual mixed-dtype AlgoGetHeuristic, selected immutable algorithm and destroy-on-failure path. Rank-2 uses one run. Keep the 32MiB heuristic workspace cap, record actual result.workspaceSize, and use caller-supplied per-Invocation workspace. The submission path must only enqueue the selected matmul; no lazy heuristic, new cast allocation or private score/weight cache.
minimal_provider_change.bounds: No algorithm is a real unsupported/resource-declined outcome and should leave other providers eligible. Retain current accepted-prefix errors, CUDA context ownership, caller buffer/Completion lifetime and capture constraints. Vendor-private storage remains an unknown bound as documented; a workspace cap is not a full-process peak-memory guarantee.
